narrative.overview:
The Ivory Vow Folio treats the invitation as a vertical piece of wedding stationery brought to life by portrait photography. Ivory paper, black ink, oxblood ceremony lettering, formal hairline rules, and the authored ribbon mark create an intimate printed world; the interface refuses generic app chrome so the couple and the invitation remain the only protagonists.

The system is formal but tender, with generous vertical pacing, a dense two-family composition, and type that shifts deliberately between Bodoni formality, Cormorant Garamond ceremony titles, Alex Brush intimacy, and Noto Serif fact. A traditional Vietnamese red-brocade cover forms the threshold: cloud linework, a woven ivory ribbon, ceremonial gold, and a deep-red square Song Hỷ card establish the ritual before the panels part to reveal the folio. After entry, a sparse field of drifting blush petals and restrained one-time section reveals adds air without competing with the content.
keyCharacteristics: Portrait-led first viewport with upper-left save-the-date copy.
Ivory paper and black ink punctuated by rare oxblood ceremony lettering.
Formal Bodoni display type, intimate Alex Brush names, and readable Noto Serif details.
A true ivory semicircle and authored ribbon mark as the signature silhouettes.
Red-brocade split-door cover owns the opening motion; drifting petals and one-time section reveals provide a quiet post-entry rhythm.

rules.name: The Ink-and-Wine Rule
rules.body: Black ink carries information; oxblood carries ceremony. Do not reverse those responsibilities or spread oxblood across ordinary body copy.

rules.name: The Paper Rule
rules.body: Ivory is the default surface. Pure white appears only as legible copy over photography, never as a generic card background.

rules.name: The Brocade Threshold Rule
rules.body: Saturated brocade red and ceremonial gold belong to the opening cover; once the panels part, return to the established oxblood, ivory, and black-ink folio palette.

rules.name: The Four Voices Rule
rules.body: Bodoni speaks formality and time, Cormorant Garamond speaks the principal ceremony title, Alex Brush speaks affection, and Noto Serif speaks fact; never collapse these roles into one family.

rules.name: The Uppercase Restraint Rule
rules.body: Reserve uppercase for formal English and Vietnamese labels. Names in script and family addresses retain natural casing.

rules.name: The Paired-Families Rule
rules.body: Bride and groom information remains a balanced two-column pair at every shipped breakpoint; compression changes spacing and type size, not the narrative order.

rules.name: The One-Shadow Rule
rules.body: Only the complete folio lifts from the desktop canvas; sections, portraits, arches, and decorative marks remain shadowless.

rules.name: The Singular Curve Rule
rules.body: The arch belongs to the hero title and the irregular radius belongs to petals; do not turn either into a generic card radius.

rules.name: The Threshold Motion Rule
rules.body: Keep motion sparse and atmospheric: split both brocade panels outward, let blush petals drift, reveal each section once, and honor reduced motion.

dos: Do preserve the portrait-led first viewport, upper-left save-the-date lockup, and true bottom semicircle meeting the image-paper boundary as one opening composition.
Do use Bodoni for ceremony, Alex Brush for affection, and Noto Serif for factual Vietnamese copy.
Do keep oxblood rare and intentional against ivory paper and black ink.
Do maintain the permanent two-column family pair while compressing spacing and type at narrow widths.
Do keep paper grain, ribbon marks, and folio typography static while the dedicated petal and section-reveal layers move around them.
Do let the red-brocade cover establish the ritual first: cloud linework, ivory ribbon, ceremonial gold, and Song Hỷ remain centered at both mobile and desktop sizes.
donts: Don't introduce generic app bars, dashboards, floating controls, or card grids into the folio world.
Don't animate ribbons, photographs, or type, and don't loop factual content; only the cover, drifting petals, and one-time section reveals own motion.
Don't flatten the cover into an ivory card or substitute generic patterns, icons, or rounded app surfaces for the brocade split-door treatment.
Don't replace the authored Bow Mark with a library icon or emoji.
Don't round portrait corners or reuse the hero arch as a generic container shape.
Don't add internal section shadows; the complete desktop folio owns the only structural shadow.
